# File Upload

The uploading experience: a drag-and-drop dropzone, a browse trigger, import shortcuts and built-in accept, size and count validation. Pairs with File Card for the resulting rows and per-file progress.

```tsx
<Field required>
  <FieldLabel>Upload image</FieldLabel>
  <FileUpload multiple accept="image/*,.pdf,.zip" onFiles={addItems}>
    <FileUploadDropzone>
      <FileUploadIcon />
      <FileUploadTitle>
        Drag and drop your files, or <FileUploadLink />
      </FileUploadTitle>
      <FileUploadTrigger className="w-full">Upload files</FileUploadTrigger>
    </FileUploadDropzone>

    <FileUploadList>
      {items.map((it) => (
        <FileCard key={it.id} state={it.status}>
          <FileCardIcon type={it.type} />
          <FileCardContent>
            <FileCardName>{it.name}</FileCardName>
            {it.status === "uploading" ? (
              <FileCardProgress value={it.progress} hideValue />
            ) : (
              <FileCardMeta>{formatBytes(it.size)}</FileCardMeta>
            )}
          </FileCardContent>
          {it.status === "uploading" && <FileCardValue>{it.progress}%</FileCardValue>}
          <FileCardActions>
            <FileCardStatus />
            <Button variant="ghost" size="sm" iconOnly aria-label="Remove" onClick={() => removeItem(it.id)}>
              <Trash />
            </Button>
          </FileCardActions>
        </FileCard>
      ))}
    </FileUploadList>
  </FileUpload>
</Field>
```

## Installation

```bash
# One-time setup (tokens + lib helpers)
npx koalaui-cli init

# Add this component (its dependencies come along)
npx koalaui-cli add file-upload
```

Manual: run `npm install @phosphor-icons/react radix-ui tailwind-variants tailwind-merge`, then copy the source into `components/ui/file-upload/` and adjust the import paths to your project. Components pull `cn` from `lib/utils`, the `tv` wrapper from `lib/tv`, and (for multi-part components) `createContext` from `lib/create-context`.

## Usage

File Upload owns *selection*: it emits accepted files through `onFiles` and rejections through `onReject`, and you own the list. Render the resulting rows with [File Card](https://koala-ui.vercel.app/docs/components/file-card.md) inside a `FileUploadList` - the two compose into the full experience.

```tsx title="uploader.tsx"
import {
  FileUpload,
  FileUploadDropzone,
  FileUploadIcon,
  FileUploadTitle,
  FileUploadLink,
  FileUploadTrigger,
  FileUploadList,
  formatBytes,
} from "@/components/ui/file-upload"
import {
  FileCard,
  FileCardIcon,
  FileCardContent,
  FileCardName,
  FileCardMeta,
  fileTypeFromName,
} from "@/components/ui/file-card"

export function Uploader() {
  const [files, setFiles] = React.useState<File[]>([])
  return (
    <FileUpload multiple onFiles={(f) => setFiles((prev) => [...prev, ...f])}>
      <FileUploadDropzone>
        <FileUploadIcon />
        <FileUploadTitle>
          Drag and drop your files, or <FileUploadLink />
        </FileUploadTitle>
        <FileUploadTrigger className="w-full">Upload files</FileUploadTrigger>
      </FileUploadDropzone>

      <FileUploadList>
        {files.map((file, i) => (
          <FileCard key={i}>
            <FileCardIcon type={fileTypeFromName(file.name)} />
            <FileCardContent>
              <FileCardName>{file.name}</FileCardName>
              <FileCardMeta>{formatBytes(file.size)}</FileCardMeta>
            </FileCardContent>
          </FileCard>
        ))}
      </FileUploadList>
    </FileUpload>
  )
}
```

## Anatomy

The `FileUpload` root holds a hidden file input and the shared state; the `FileUploadDropzone` is the dashed drop surface, filled with a `FileUploadIcon`, a `FileUploadTitle` with the `FileUploadLink` sitting inline in the sentence, and a `FileUploadTrigger` (or a `FileUploadSources` row).

The panel is a drop target, not a button. Clicking anywhere on it still opens the picker, but the keyboard path runs through the real controls inside it, so **every dropzone must compose a `FileUploadLink` or a `FileUploadTrigger`**. A `role="button"` panel wrapping those would be a nested-interactive violation and would swallow their Enter/Space.

```tsx
<FileUpload onFiles={handleFiles}>
  <FileUploadDropzone>
    <FileUploadIcon />
    <FileUploadTitle>
      Drag and drop your files, or <FileUploadLink />
    </FileUploadTitle>
    <FileUploadTrigger className="w-full">Upload files</FileUploadTrigger>
  </FileUploadDropzone>
</FileUpload>
```

## Import shortcuts

The local disk isn’t the only place a file lives. Introduce a `FileUploadSources` row with a labelled [Divider](https://koala-ui.vercel.app/docs/components/divider.md) and give each provider a `FileUploadSource` tile. A source owns its own picker - an OAuth flow, a provider SDK, your own modal - so it takes a `onClick` and deliberately does *not* route back into the native file dialog.

The mark is `children`, not a `brand` prop: pass whatever you own - a real logo, an `img`, or a Phosphor glyph.

```tsx
<FileUpload multiple onFiles={handleFiles}>
  <FileUploadDropzone>
    <FileUploadIcon />
    <FileUploadTitle>
      Drag and drop your files, or <FileUploadLink />
    </FileUploadTitle>

    {/* `static`: the smart Divider would otherwise collapse between two blocks */}
    <Divider static>Or import from</Divider>

    <FileUploadSources>
      {SOURCES.map((brand) => (
        <FileUploadSource key={brand.name} label={brand.name} onClick={() => connect(brand)}>
          <BrandLogo brand={brand} className="size-5" />
        </FileUploadSource>
      ))}
    </FileUploadSources>
  </FileUploadDropzone>
</FileUpload>
```

## Thumbnail layout

When the upload *is* the picture, a filename row gets in the way. Swap `FileUploadList` for `FileUploadGrid` and give each File Card `layout="tile"`: the thumbnail fills the square and `FileCardActions` become a scrim that fades in on hover or keyboard focus. The tile never moves - the photo and the scrim carry the whole interaction.

```tsx
<Lightbox images={shots}>
  <FileUploadGrid>
    {shots.map((shot, i) => (
      <FileCard key={shot.src} layout="tile">
        <FileCardThumbnail src={shot.src} alt={shot.alt} />
        <FileCardActions>
          <Button variant="ghost" size="sm" iconOnly aria-label="Delete"
            tone="onMedia"
            onClick={() => remove(shot)}>
            <Trash />
          </Button>
          <LightboxTrigger asChild index={i}>
            <Button variant="ghost" size="sm" iconOnly aria-label="Preview"
              tone="onMedia">
              <Eye />
            </Button>
          </LightboxTrigger>
        </FileCardActions>
      </FileCard>
    ))}
  </FileUploadGrid>
</Lightbox>
```

## Row states

A row in flight reads either way. Put the bar under the name with `<FileCardProgress hideValue />` and move the percentage out to a `FileCardValue` on the right edge; or drop the bar for a plain `FileCardMeta` line when the pause and cancel controls matter more than the number. Once it lands, `FileCardStatus` reads the card’s `state` and lights the check on its own.

```tsx
{/* In flight - bar under the name, percentage on the right edge */}
<FileCard state="uploading">
  <FileCardIcon><ImageSquare /></FileCardIcon>
  <FileCardContent>
    <FileCardName>KoalaUIFinalDesign.jpg</FileCardName>
    <FileCardProgress value={60} hideValue />
  </FileCardContent>
  <FileCardValue>60%</FileCardValue>
</FileCard>

{/* In flight - controls instead of a bar */}
<FileCard state="uploading">
  <FileCardIcon><ImageSquare /></FileCardIcon>
  <FileCardContent>
    <FileCardName>KoalaUIFinalDesign.jpg</FileCardName>
    <FileCardMeta>182.2 MB · 60%</FileCardMeta>
  </FileCardContent>
  <FileCardActions>
    <Button variant="ghost" size="sm" iconOnly aria-label="Pause upload"><Pause /></Button>
    <Button variant="ghost" size="sm" iconOnly aria-label="Cancel upload"><X /></Button>
  </FileCardActions>
</FileCard>

{/* Landed */}
<FileCard state="success">
  <FileCardIcon><ImageSquare /></FileCardIcon>
  <FileCardContent>
    <FileCardName>KoalaUIFinalDesign.jpg</FileCardName>
    <FileCardMeta>182.2 MB</FileCardMeta>
  </FileCardContent>
  <FileCardStatus />
</FileCard>
```

## Browse button

No room for a dropzone? Drop a `FileUploadTrigger` on its own - it opens the same picker, so an attach action is a single button. The trigger reuses the DS [Button](https://koala-ui.vercel.app/docs/components/button.md), so it inherits every variant, size, and the press scale.

```tsx
<FileUpload accept=".pdf,.doc,.docx" onFiles={(f) => setName(f[0]?.name)}>
  <div className="flex items-center gap-3">
    <FileUploadTrigger><Paperclip />Attach a file</FileUploadTrigger>
    <span className="text-sm text-muted-foreground">{name ?? "No file selected"}</span>
  </div>
</FileUpload>
```

## Avatar picker

Compose the trigger with an [Avatar](https://koala-ui.vercel.app/docs/components/avatar.md) for a profile-photo picker: a single-file `image/*` upload that swaps the avatar in place, with a “Change photo” / “Remove” pair.

```tsx
<FileUpload accept="image/*" onFiles={pick}>
  <div className="flex items-center gap-4">
    <AvatarRoot size="xl">
      {url && <AvatarImage src={url} alt="Profile photo" />}
      <AvatarFallback>JC</AvatarFallback>
    </AvatarRoot>
    <div className="flex flex-col gap-2">
      <div className="flex items-center gap-2">
        <FileUploadTrigger size="sm" swapKey={url ? "change" : "upload"}>
          {url ? "Change photo" : "Upload photo"}
        </FileUploadTrigger>
        {url && <Button variant="ghost" size="sm" onClick={remove}>Remove</Button>}
      </div>
      <p className="text-xs text-muted-foreground">JPG, GIF or PNG. 2 MB max.</p>
    </div>
  </div>
</FileUpload>
```

## Validation

Pass `accept`, `maxSize` (bytes), and `multiple`, and dropped or picked files are split for you: `onFiles` gets the keepers, `onReject` gets the rest with a `reason` (`type`, `size`, or `count`) so you can surface a precise message.

```tsx
<FileUpload
  accept=".pdf"
  maxSize={2 * 1024 * 1024}
  onFiles={(accepted) => setFiles((prev) => [...prev, ...accepted])}
  onReject={(rejections) => {
    const r = rejections[0]
    setError(
      r.reason === "size" ? `${r.file.name} is too large - 2 MB max.`
      : r.reason === "type" ? `${r.file.name} isn't a PDF.`
      : "Only one file at a time.",
    )
  }}
>
  <FileUploadDropzone>
    <FileUploadIcon><FilePdf /></FileUploadIcon>
    <FileUploadTitle>Drop a PDF here, or <FileUploadLink /></FileUploadTitle>
    <FileUploadDescription>Single PDF file, up to 2 MB</FileUploadDescription>
  </FileUploadDropzone>
  {error && <p className="text-xs text-destructive">{error}</p>}
</FileUpload>
```

## Density

Density is Koala’s cross-cutting spacing axis (see [Density](https://koala-ui.vercel.app/docs/foundations/density.md)). For File Upload it tunes the dropzone padding, the rhythm between its blocks, and the glyph. Density resolves prop → nearest `DensityProvider` → `compact`, so an unset dropzone renders compact; ask for `comfortable` to get the roomy panel.

```tsx
<FileUpload density="comfortable">…</FileUpload>
<FileUpload density="compact">…</FileUpload>
```

## Disabled

Pass `disabled` to the root and the whole control goes inert - the dropzone stops accepting drops and clicks, the link, trigger and sources disable, and the surface dims.

```tsx
<FileUpload disabled>
  <FileUploadDropzone>
    <FileUploadIcon />
    <FileUploadTitle>Uploads paused</FileUploadTitle>
    <FileUploadDescription>You've reached your storage limit</FileUploadDescription>
    <FileUploadTrigger className="w-full">Upload files</FileUploadTrigger>
  </FileUploadDropzone>
</FileUpload>
```

## API reference

`FileUpload` forwards `div` props and adds `accept`, `multiple`, `maxSize` (bytes), `disabled`, `density` (`comfortable | compact`), `onFiles(files)`, and `onReject(rejections)` (each rejection is `{ file, reason }`).

`FileUploadDropzone` forwards `div` props and renders the drop surface. `FileUploadLink` and `FileUploadTrigger` both open the picker - the first as inline sentence text, the second as a [Button](https://koala-ui.vercel.app/docs/components/button.md) (defaulting to `outline`). `FileUploadSource` takes a `label` plus the provider mark as `children`, and forwards `button` props. `FileUploadIcon`, `FileUploadTitle`, `FileUploadDescription`, `FileUploadSources`, `FileUploadList`, and `FileUploadGrid` forward their element props. The helper `formatBytes(bytes)` renders a human file size for the meta line. Every part accepts `className`, merged last.

## FAQ

### Does File Upload store the selected files for me?

No. It owns selection only: accepted files arrive through `onFiles` and rejections through `onReject`, and you keep the list in your own state. Render that list with File Card inside `FileUploadList` (or `FileUploadGrid` for thumbnails).

### How do I reject files that are too big or the wrong type?

Pass `accept`, `maxSize` (in bytes), and `multiple` to the `FileUpload` root and dropped or picked files are split for you. The keepers go to `onFiles`; the rest go to `onReject` as `{ file, reason }` where reason is `type`, `size`, or `count`.

### Can I use a single button instead of the full dropzone?

Yes. Drop a `FileUploadTrigger` on its own without a `FileUploadDropzone`. It opens the same picker and extends our Button, so it inherits every variant and size (it defaults to `outline`).

### Is the dropzone keyboard accessible?

Through the controls inside it. The panel itself is a drop target rather than a button - a `role="button"` wrapper around the link, trigger and source tiles would be a nested-interactive violation and would swallow their Enter/Space. So compose at least one `FileUploadLink` or `FileUploadTrigger`: that is the keyboard path to the picker.

### What are the import shortcuts for?

`FileUploadSources` + `FileUploadSource` surface the other places a file can come from (Drive, Dropbox, a repo). Each tile is a plain button you wire to that provider's own picker; they do not open the native file dialog.

### How do I show uploaded images as a grid instead of rows?

Use `FileUploadGrid` in place of `FileUploadList` and give each File Card `layout="tile"`. The thumbnail fills the square cell and `FileCardActions` become a scrim that fades in on hover or focus.

### How do I make the whole control inert?

Pass `disabled` to the `FileUpload` root. The dropzone stops accepting drops and clicks, the link, trigger and source tiles disable, and the surface dims.

### How do I tune the dropzone padding for a dense form?

Set `density` to `compact` on the root (the default is `comfortable`), which tightens the dropzone padding, the rhythm between its blocks, and the glyph. Set it per instance or for a whole subtree with `DensityProvider`.

## Exports and dependencies

`npx koalaui-cli add file-upload` writes `components/ui/file-upload/`. Import from `@/components/ui/file-upload`:

- Components and helpers: `FileUpload`, `FileUploadDropzone`, `FileUploadIcon`, `FileUploadTitle`, `FileUploadDescription`, `FileUploadLink`, `FileUploadTrigger`, `FileUploadSources`, `FileUploadSource`, `FileUploadList`, `FileUploadGrid`, `fileUploadVariants`, `formatBytes`
- Types: `FileUploadProps`, `FileUploadDropzoneProps`, `FileUploadIconProps`, `FileUploadLinkProps`, `FileUploadTriggerProps`, `FileUploadSourcesProps`, `FileUploadSourceProps`, `FileUploadListProps`, `FileUploadGridProps`, `FileRejection`, `FileRejectionReason`
- Koala components it installs with it: `button`
- Koala lib helpers it uses: `create-context`, `density`, `tv`
- npm packages: `@phosphor-icons/react`
